newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds continue slide, spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds continue slide, spreads narrow.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities investors remained on the sidelines on Thursday, even as Treasuries continued their selloff from Wednesday, mortgage experts said.
Mortgages were off 1/32 to 7/32 overall by late afternoon. Spreads narrowed a few basis points, however, since comparable Treasuries were off 9/32 to 12/32.
"I've seen prices drop, but I haven't seen a whole lot of selling going on," one trader said.
There were "a lot of people watching for it (a mortgage selloff), but I haven't seen it yet," he said.
The trader was referring to an argument made recently by several analysts that mortgage-backeds -- particularly higher-coupon issues -- are rich in light of the decline in Treasuries prices.

"It's all very directional," said Cynthia Rivera, mortgage strategist at BZW Securities Inc. "Shorter-duration securities, such as higher-coupon mortgages and Treasuries below three-years, usually outperform those that have longer durations" when the market sells off.
She said investors take larger positions in short-duration paper, making those coupons expensive.
In specific coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was 6/32 lower at 99-27/32, yielding 101 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were off 6/32 as well, at 99-24/32 and 99-30/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was down 11/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
